sessions.phase_label: Creative brief and initial wordmark direction
Hero V selection and V-system development

requirements.title: Hero V Geometry
requirements.definition: The opening Hero V must be a proprietary, standalone-capable letterform whose two arms form one balanced, timeless, architectural silhouette.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers the core Hero V silhouette, arm relationship, vertex, proportions, and stance as one tightly coupled letterform. The reusable terminal edge treatment is separated because it later evolves independently and is propagated to other glyphs.

requirements.title: Second V Glyph Geometry
requirements.definition: The second V must be a supporting Vellvé-specific glyph that carries the Hero V's architectural DNA and signature right-arm character without competing with it.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers construction of the second V itself, including proportional-scaling versus optical-drawing decisions. Its vertical position relative to other letters is independently adjustable and belongs to REQ_SECOND_V_HIERARCHY.

requirements.title: Literal É Accent Derivation
requirements.definition: The É accent must reuse the exact vector geometry of the Hero V right-arm termination rather than being a visually similar or separately interpreted accent.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers the literal one-to-one vector derivation rule. The accent's vertical peak alignment is separate because derivation and placement can succeed or fail independently.

requirements.title: Shared Signature Terminal Treatment
requirements.definition: The signature right-arm ending must use a restrained, architectural, precision-crafted terminal treatment applied consistently to the Hero V, second V, and É accent.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers the independently explored terminal profile and material-like edge treatment, not the complete geometry of any one V or the accent's placement.

requirements.title: Architectural E and L Letterforms
requirements.definition: The E and L glyphs must be bespoke, restrained architectural forms that belong to the same proprietary alphabet as the Hero V and avoid Roman flares or stock-typeface character.
requirements.boundary_note: E and L remain one Requirement because the history consistently develops them together under one architectural construction language. Their scale and cap-height relationship are handled separately.

requirements.title: All-Caps VELLVÉ Wordmark
requirements.definition: The primary complete VELLVÉ wordmark must initially use an all-caps treatment to support the intended architectural rhythm.
requirements.boundary_note: Case treatment can change independently of glyph geometry, spacing, or material treatment and is therefore retained as its own Requirement.

requirements.title: Second V Visual Hierarchy
requirements.definition: Within the wordmark, the second V must act as a quiet echo: subtly above the E and L cap height while remaining below the Hero V and É accent.
requirements.boundary_note: Separates the second V's wordmark placement and prominence from its glyph construction because the two repeatedly fail and change independently.

requirements.title: Hero V and É Accent Peak Alignment
requirements.definition: The highest point of the É accent must align exactly on the same horizontal plane as the highest point of the Hero V's right arm.
requirements.boundary_note: This is an independently verifiable spatial relationship, distinct from whether the accent uses the correct vector geometry.

requirements.title: E and L Cap-Height Scale
requirements.definition: The E and L glyphs must be scaled so their cap height harmonizes with the second V's left arm while preserving the intended hierarchy.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers relative glyph scale only; it does not own E/L construction, second-V geometry, or baseline placement.

requirements.title: Common Wordmark Baseline
requirements.definition: The bottom points of both Vs and the feet of the E and L glyphs must sit on a common baseline.
requirements.boundary_note: Baseline alignment is independently adjustable and testable, so it is not merged into general kerning or second-V hierarchy.

requirements.title: Cohesive Wordmark Kerning
requirements.definition: The optical spacing must make VELLVÉ read as one cohesive word while retaining refined, luxurious breathing room.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers letter-pair spacing and reading rhythm, not glyph shapes, cap-height relationships, or material treatment.

requirements.title: Champagne Gold Material Treatment
requirements.definition: The wordmark must support a warm, refined champagne-gold treatment whose finish and distribution convey subtle luxury rather than flashiness.
requirements.boundary_note: Finish type and gold distribution are attributes of one material-treatment mechanism. They are not merged with the black silhouette or letterform geometry.

requirements.title: Production-Ready Design Asset Package
requirements.definition: The final handoff must provide editable vector/source files, presentation boards, exported artwork, and the required production-ready format and color variants.
requirements.boundary_note: Treats file formats and included handoff artifacts as attributes of one delivery package rather than separate Requirements. It remains active after design revisions are stopped.

requirements.title: Wordmark Variants With and Without Tagline
requirements.definition: The delivered identity package must include wordmark versions both with and without the "Wellness elevated." tagline.
requirements.boundary_note: This is an independently usable output variant explicitly stated in the project brief, but no supplied message candidate develops its lifecycle.

requirements.title: Design Rationale With Review Rounds
requirements.definition: Each substantive design round must include a brief explanation of the design intention or problem explored so the client can evaluate the concepts meaningfully.
requirements.boundary_note: This is a concrete review artifact repeatedly requested and implemented, not a generic testing or project-status Requirement.

requirements.title: Mac-Viewable Proof Attachments
requirements.definition: Design proofs sent for review must use a directly viewable chat image, JPG, or PNG format rather than inaccessible JFIF attachments.
requirements.boundary_note: The review-file compatibility behavior is independently required even when the underlying design is correct; repeated inaccessible attachments are execution evidence for this target.

requirements.title: Reference-Line and Clean-Art Review Layout
requirements.definition: Terminal-review presentations must show each option in two columns: one with the required hierarchy reference lines and one with identical artwork free of guides.
requirements.boundary_note: This is a specifically requested review deliverable with its own implementation and failure trajectory, separate from the terminal design itself.

unresolved_candidates.description: The project brief requires tagline and multiple export/color variants, but the supplied message history contains no observable development of the tagline variant. Its lifecycle may contain no extractable message Events.
